text: Why did programs stop getting faster on their own around 2005?
choices: Compilers reached the limit of the optimizations they could apply to sequential code.
Memory latency stopped improving, so faster processors would have spent all their time waiting.
Transistor densities stopped improving, ending Moore's law and with it all further gains.
Power dissipation rises sharply with clock frequency, so frequencies plateaued and transistors were spent on cores instead.
explanation: A chip at 10 GHz would need cooling no consumer device can carry, so clocks have sat between 3 and 5 GHz for twenty years. Manufacturers had transistors and no way to spend them on speed, so they spent them on cores — 24 on the machine these measurements were taken on. A sequential program there uses one twenty-fourth of the machine, and using the rest is now the programmer's problem.
